title: Stochastic Physics Extensions — Core Engine Variability
brief: Add Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, material property scatter, and stochastic extensions to the 6 highest-impact deterministic physics engines. Each engine gets: (1) input parameter distributions, (2) N-trial MC sampling, (3) output confidence intervals, (4) sensitivity indices (Sobol Si/STi).

units.title: StochasticCuttingForceEngine — Kienzle/Oxley with material scatter
units.description: Extend cutting force prediction with stochastic inputs. Material property scatter: kc1.1 CV=8-12%, mc CV=5-8%, yield stress CV=10-15%, friction angle CV=15-20%. Tool geometry scatter: rake angle ±0.5°, edge radius ±5μm, runout ±3μm. Monte Carlo with Latin Hypercube Sampling (N=1000-10000). Outputs: force distribution (mean, σ, CI_95, CI_99), P(force > limit), Sobol sensitivity indices for each input. Analytical FOSM (First-Order Second Moment) for fast approximation. Compare MC vs FOSM accuracy.
exit_conditions: MC with LHS for force distributions

units.title: StochasticToolLifeEngine — Taylor/extended with Weibull scatter
units.description: Extend tool life prediction with stochastic wear. Taylor constants scatter: C CV=15-25%, n CV=10-15% (from published data). Weibull life distribution: shape β=2-4 (infant mortality to wear-out). Stochastic wear progression: Wiener process dW = μdt + σdB (connect to existing StochasticProcessEngine). N-trial MC: tool life distribution, P(survive T minutes), optimal replacement time under uncertainty. Bayesian updating: incorporate observed wear data to narrow posterior. Compare deterministic Taylor vs stochastic predictions.

units.title: StochasticThermalEngine — Convection uncertainty + thermal property scatter
units.description: Extend thermal prediction with stochastic heat transfer. Convection coefficient h uncertainty: flood h=500-2000 W/m²K (log-normal), MQL h=50-200, dry h=10-50. Thermal conductivity scatter: ±5-10% per alloy batch. Chip-tool heat partition: 0.3-0.7 (Beta distribution). Jaeger/Loewen-Shaw models with MC propagation. Outputs: temperature distribution at tool-chip interface, P(temp > coating limit), thermal damage risk score. Include sensitivity: which uncertainty dominates (h vs k vs partition)?
exit_conditions: Log-normal h distribution by coolant type
Tests against analytical 1D solutions with known variance

units.title: StochasticSurfaceFinishEngine — Vibration + BUE + wear uncertainty
units.description: Extend surface finish prediction with real-world scatter sources. Theoretical Ra = f²/(32r) is deterministic. Real scatter sources: (1) vibration-induced roughness addition ΔRa ~ N(0, σ_vib) from runout + chatter proximity, (2) BUE formation probability P(BUE) function of speed/material, adds 0.2-1.0 μm, (3) tool wear effect: Ra increases ~15% per 0.1mm VB growth, VB itself stochastic. Combined model: Ra_actual = Ra_theoretical + ΔRa_vibration + ΔRa_BUE + ΔRa_wear. MC with correlated inputs (vibration correlates with force). Outputs: Ra distribution, P(Ra > tolerance), Cpk for surface finish.
exit_conditions: Combined Ra model (theory + vib + BUE + wear)
Correlated MC inputs (Nataf transform or Cholesky)
P(Ra > tolerance) for given Rz spec
Cpk/Ppk for surface finish process capability
Tests: deterministic limit (zero scatter = theoretical Ra)

units.title: StochasticChatterEngine — Probabilistic stability lobes
units.description: Replace deterministic stability lobe boundaries with probability contours. Uncertain inputs: damping ratio ζ CV=30-50%, natural frequency fn CV=2-5%, cutting force coefficient Kc CV=8-12%, process damping CV=20-40%. MC over stability lobe computation: for each (speed, depth) point, compute P(stable) from N trials. Output: probability contour map P(chatter)=0.01/0.05/0.10/0.50. Identify 'safe' operating zone where P(chatter)<1%. Include tool-holder assembly variation (different clamping = different FRF). Bayesian updating: tap test data narrows uncertainty.
exit_conditions: Bayesian updating from tap test FRF data
Tests: deterministic limit matches existing chatter engine

units.title: UncertaintyPropagationPipeline — Cross-engine chaining
units.description: Build the architectural glue that chains uncertainty through multiple engines. Pipeline: Material(μ,σ) → StochasticForce(dist) → StochasticDeflection(dist) → StochasticFinish(dist) → ToleranceStackup(dist). Uses existing UncertaintyQuantificationEngine as propagation kernel. Each engine-to-engine interface passes distributions (not point values). Supports: (1) MC propagation (accurate, slow), (2) FOSM/linearization (fast, approximate), (3) Polynomial Chaos Expansion (medium, spectral). Single action: `uncertainty_pipeline` in calcDispatcher. Inputs: pipeline stages + uncertain parameters. Output: final distribution + per-stage contribution breakdown.
exit_conditions: Tests: pipeline output matches manual stage-by-stage MC
Performance: PCE 10x faster than MC for smooth models
